blocks.text: A CSS pseudo-class is a keyword that can be added to a selector, to define a style for a special state of an element.

items: Style an element when a user moves the mouse over it
Style visited and unvisited links differently
Style an element when it gets focus
Style an element that is the first child of its parent

blocks.text: Pseudo-classes are always denoted by a single colon (:) followed by the pseudo-class name:
Interactive pseudo-classes apply styles based on user interaction:

items: :hover - When mouse is over an element
:active - When an element is being activated

blocks.text: Structural pseudo-classes select elements based on their position in the document tree:

items: :nth-child(n) - The nth child of a parent

blocks.text: For a complete list of all CSS Pseudo-classes, visit our CSS Pseudo-classes Reference.
